messages:
zoe: heads-up: ran into a weird logging/redaction oddity in the TS SDK retry wrapper while onboarding the express quickstart. Debug logs show two different request IDs (one unredacted) for the same incoming request.

ryan: can you paste the smallest repro + logs?

zoe: repro: clone github.com/redwood/sample-apps/node-telemetry, set LOG_LEVEL=debug, use the built-in auth flow that retries token refresh on 401. Trigger POST /upload. Snippet: 
```
[DEBUG] retry-wrapper - attempt=1 reqid=tmp-req-7 auth=Bearer abcdef12345
[DEBUG] auth.middleware - parsed token - reqid=tmp-req-7
[INFO] app.upload - reqid=REDACTED auth=REDACTED
[DEBUG] retry-wrapper - attempt=2 reqid=tmp-req-7
```
Notice attempt=1 log shows the raw token and the reqid before our redaction middleware ran for that request. The INFO line is correct.

anika: interesting. Is the retry wrapper logging request headers directly or using the SDK's logger?

zoe: it's using the SDK's internal debug log (sdk.debug) from inside the fetch wrapper. But the wrapper is required by auth flow and runs before the app-level redaction middleware because the SDK auto-initializes when imported by early modules. In dev mode imports can run before express middleware is mounted.

ryan: so ordering + where the log is emitted matters. Two obvious fixes: (1) make the SDK retry wrapper avoid logging sensitive headers (or scrub them), (2) ensure SDK init registers redaction filters synchronously and documents init ordering so the wrapper's logs are filtered.

anika: I think we should treat retry logs as non-authoritative for request context. Options: remove token from retry debug logs entirely, and log only attempt numbers + anonymized reqid (hash), or call into telemetry.redact() helper before logging. Also add a flag to enable verbose retry logs for dev only (opt-in).

zoe: agreed. Quick patch I tested: change retry wrapper log to: `sdk.debug('retry', {attempt, anon_reqid: shortHash(reqid)})` and remove printing headers. That stops leaks and keeps useful telemetry for debugging.

ryan: can we also add a safeguard in telemetry.init() that if any SDK internal logger is present it attaches the redaction filter to it? That would catch imports-before-middleware cases.

anika: we can. Implement two small changes: 1) SDK: scrub headers in retry/debug paths and prefer anonymous reqid, 2) SDK: during init, idempotently attach redaction filter to internal SDK loggers and known fetch wrappers. Also update quickstart docs to recommend `require('redwood-telemetry').init()` as the very first line.

sdk-bot: Draft PR created: github.com/redwood/sdk/pull/812 - "TS SDK: scrub retry logs and attach redaction filter on init". CI queued.

telemetry-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/1964 12 "SDK retry wrapper debug logs reveal tokens/reqids before redaction; scrub retry logs + init-time filter" Labels: devex, telemetry, bug.

zoe: thanks. I'll update the quickstart branch with the new SDK version and add a tiny unit test that simulates an early import and asserts no raw token appears in captured logs even with LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG.

ryan: nice. Also add a short line in the onboarding doc: "If you import SDKs in modules that run at require-time, call telemetry.init() as early as possible to ensure redaction filters attach before internal debug logs run."

anika: we should also do an audit of other SDK debug paths (batching, cache, compilation) to ensure none print sensitive headers. I'll spin up a follow-up issue after this PR merges.

zoe: sounds good, will link tests and PR to the issue. Thanks :thumbsup:
